name: chirp
description: Microsoft Teams chats and channels in a sidebar of their own, each conversation an editor tab, with its text available to the AI agent beside it. Not affiliated with Microsoft.

commands.title: Teams: Copy the Admin Approval Link
Teams: Use a Company Microsoft App…
Teams: Copy Sign-in Code and Open the Sign-in Page

enumDescriptions: A token file if one is set, otherwise the editor's Microsoft sign-in, otherwise a sign-in code. With a company app (teams.signIn.clientId), the sign-in code comes first.
The editor's own Microsoft account sign-in, using chirp's app (or the company app in teams.signIn.clientId).
A code you enter at microsoft.com/devicelogin; chirp keeps the tokens in the editor's secret storage.
Reuse the login another tool keeps in a token file (teams.signIn.tokenFile).
teams.signIn.method.description: How chirp signs in to Microsoft. See the README's "Signing in" section.

teams.signIn.tokenFile.description: A token file another tool keeps (JSON with access_token, refresh_token, client_id, tenant_id, expires_at). When set, chirp reuses that login instead of signing in itself. chirp refreshes it in place and never deletes it.

teams.signIn.clientId.markdownDescription: The Application (client) ID of your company's own Microsoft app for Teams, if it has one: your IT team provides it. Empty: chirp's own app. Use it when your company lets only its admins approve apps and has approved its own. Its registration must allow public client flows for the sign-in code (`deviceCode`), and accept VS Code's redirect for the editor's sign-in (`editor`); with it set, `auto` uses the sign-in code first. Set it, and `#teams.signIn.tenant#`, with **Teams: Use a Company Microsoft App…**. A value that isn't an ID is ignored (with a note in the Teams view). Not used with a token file.

teams.signIn.tenant.markdownDescription: Your company's Directory (tenant) ID, or its domain such as `contoso.onmicrosoft.com`: your IT team provides it, with `#teams.signIn.clientId#`. Empty: `organizations`, any work or school account. A value that is neither is ignored (with a note in the Teams view). Not used with a token file.

teams.agentFiles.description: Write each open conversation to ~/.chirp as plain text (files readable only by you), so an AI agent beside chirp knows which chat is open. Off: no files, and chirp.activeConversationFile returns nothing.

scripts.check: for f in src/*.js media/*.js test/*.js; do [ -e "$f" ] || continue; node --check "$f" || exit 1; done
